title: Career roadmap · Tourism Researcher
summary: Build from tourism research methods into destination analysis, visitor behaviour, heritage management, sustainable tourism, tourism economics and evidence-based destination policy.

facts.Timeline assumption: Because the selected qualification is a Ph.D., 2026 is treated as Ph.D. Year 1. The strongest route combines rigorous social-science research with fieldwork, destination data, heritage interpretation and applied projects for governments, destinations, cultural institutions and tourism businesses.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Establish a research niche, complete rigorous field research and publish tourism/heritage studies.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Become a specialist in destination management, heritage tourism, sustainable tourism, visitor behaviour, tourism economics or cultural tourism.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead destination research programmes and advise governments, DMOs, heritage organisations and tourism businesses.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine tourism research with digital heritage, AI/data analytics, climate resilience, overtourism management and destination policy.

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

The strongest tourism researcher will connect academic research with destination decisions. Build long-term relationships with tourism ministries, destination-management organisations, heritage authorities, local communities and industry. Develop the ability to quantify visitor impacts, evaluate destination policies and communicate evidence to non-academic decision-makers. Digital visitor data, GIS, climate impacts and responsible AI should become part of the research toolkit without replacing field-based and community-centred research.
